summary.headline: Rolex Rings Q2 FY27 revenue rose 43% YoY to INR389 crore (incl. ~INR18 crore one-time US tariff refund); EBITDA margin 24.2%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR389 crore, up 43% YoY and 28% QoQ, including a one-time ~INR18 crore US tariff refund recognised as revenue. Excluding the refund, revenue grew about 32% YoY and management said EBITDA margin would be around 21%, against a reported 24.2%. Auto components grew 68% YoY to INR177 crore and now make up 54% of component sales, while bearing rings grew 6% to INR153 crore. H1 FY27 revenue rose 23% to INR694 crore, and the company remains debt-free after a INR180 crore buyback. Management reiterated its guided 21-22% operating margin range and expects H2 FY27 to be stronger than H1.

segments.name: Auto components
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR177 crore, +68% YoY; exports INR129 crore (+89%) and domestic INR48 crore (+29%). H1 INR318 crore; FY27 guided at INR550-575 crore (or INR575-600 crore per later comment) versus ~INR505 crore in FY26.

segments.name: Bearing rings
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR153 crore, +6% YoY; domestic INR115 crore (+~10% in H1 YoY, >25% YoY in Q2 per management), exports flat at INR38 crore on soft European industrial demand.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Exports INR167 crore, +55% YoY, 51% of component sales. US component revenue more than doubled YoY to INR92 crore. Europe about 23-24% of overall business.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27 revenue expected to exceed H1, supported by new programs (one new customer plant from Q3, another in early Q4), capacity ramp and new customer associations.
Monthly order book INR120-125 crore for H2 FY27; monthly revenue run rate of ~INR120 crore expected in H2, with Q4 better than Q3.
Management remains confident of the guided FY27 revenue growth (previously ~15%).
Operating margin expected to return to the guided 21-22% range as ocean freight declines from October 2026; ~50-75 bps EBITDA margin improvement expected in FY28 over FY27.
FY28 revenue growth seen moving towards high teens; FY28 order book could rise 5-7% month on month; FY29 growth of 22-23%+ indicated.
Gross margin normalised range guided at 49-53%.
Capacity utilisation 65% now, targeted at 70-72% by end-FY27; capex INR30-40 crore a year.
Working capital to partly unwind in H2 as freight normalises.
capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation ~65% for H1 FY27; management says last couple of months were at 67-68%; target 70-72% by end of FY27.
Planned capex INR30-40 crore per year.
Forging and machining facilities are fungible across bearing rings and auto components.
Two new customer plants expected to begin supply in Q3 and early Q4 FY27; ramp-up of programs won in FY26 continuing.
Defence and aerospace: initial registrations/approvals received; revenue expected over next 12-18 months, focused on round and hot forge components.
Inquiries for larger bearing rings for wind and industrial equipment from domestic market; meaningful revenue expected in FY28 rather than FY27.
demand_pricing: US component revenue more than doubled YoY to INR92 crore as customers that held back in FY26 returned; one key customer's volume, down 35-40% in FY26, is back to FY25 levels.
Management says US tariffs no longer affect the business; customers accepted the current duty structure and US order flows have normalised.
Customs duty of 25% (from November 2025) is being reimbursed by customers on lifting goods from warehouse; ~INR10-15 crore duty reimbursement in Q2, expected to continue into Q3-Q4.

Freight: ocean freight ran ~3x normal in Q2; ocean freight spend was INR25+ crore in H1 FY27 versus ~INR10 crore in H1 FY26. Contracts pass through raw material and FX but not freight; negotiations with US customers on sharing freight cost are underway.
Metal price pass-through of 100% per management, which supported gross margin.
Domestic bearing ring demand: Q1 INR86 crore to Q2 INR115 crore; one domestic customer group's revenue reduced.
Domestic market share in addressable forging segment (50 mm to 1,000 mm diameter) estimated at 30-35%.

qa_highlights.question: Scrap revenue and export incentive for Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Scrap revenue INR23 crore and export incentive INR4.2 crore (later stated INR4.4 crore).

qa_highlights.question: Why is gross margin expanding when peers report declines?
qa_highlights.answer: Richer product mix toward auto components and 100% pass-through of metal prices to customers; the duty refund also contributed.

qa_highlights.question: Will auto component exports exceed INR500 crore and what is FY27 and FY28 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 auto components expected at INR550-575 crore (excluding any Dana/Allison opportunity); at least 20-22% YoY growth in auto components in FY28 onward.

qa_highlights.question: Will the H2 order book run-rate jump?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book steady at INR120-125 crore per month; large wind components are a FY28 story, with inquiries only from domestic market; order book could rise 5-7% MoM in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Can growth reach 25-30% from FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says 25-30% is achievable with new customers starting in FY28-FY29; FY29 growth of 22-23%+ possible if trends hold, subject to geopolitical risk.

qa_highlights.question: Why is domestic bearing growth lagging peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 domestic bearing revenue up >25% YoY per management; H1 up ~10% due to one customer group's reduction; annualised growth ~10%. Full catch-up not expected immediately.

qa_highlights.question: Why is domestic auto components growth weak relative to history?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic auto components at INR48 crore in Q2 vs INR44 crore in Q1; FY26 ~INR170 crore; expects 10-12% growth as EV orders have been slow to materialise on the floor.

qa_highlights.question: What are the gross margin and freight cost trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Normalised gross margin range 49-53%; ocean freight declining since October 2026; Q2 ~21% EBITDA margin excluding refund.

risks_watch: Ocean freight and fuel cost volatility (West Asia conflict; fuel gas up ~40%); company absorbs freight, not passed through in contracts.
Working capital: INR74 crore increase in H1 leading to ~INR68 crore operating cash flow; unwinding depends on freight normalisation.
Domestic auto components volatility and delayed EV program volumes.
Duty reimbursement from customers (~INR10 crore uncollected in Q2) and the tariff-refund one-off, which inflates reported Q2 revenue and margins.
Europe industrial and bearing demand remains soft; export bearing rings flat.
Defence/aerospace and large wind bearing ring revenues are not expected until FY28; development timelines long.
Management guidance inconsistency on FY27 auto components target (INR550-575 crore vs INR575-600 crore vs INR600-625 crore).
Some US programs remain on hold by an OEM.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand, order book and FY28 growth, while being transparent that Q2 benefited from a one-time tariff refund and that freight costs compress margins. Some answers were vague or inconsistent on numbers (auto components FY27 target, domestic bearing growth, duty reimbursement quantum), and management declined to name defence/aerospace applications or market share detail.
key_quotes: Fiscal 2027 quar ter two has been the strongest quarter in the history of the company, on revenue side, on margin side, on efficiency, and profitability.
Excluding the refund, our EBITDA margin for the quarter would be around 21%.
We expect H2 FY 2027 to be stronger than H1, because of these three reasons.
Our customers have accepted the current duty structure, and order flows from the U.S. have quite normalized.
We are running at 65% capacity utilization today, and we expect to move towards 70%-72% by end of this fiscal, within our planned capex of INR30 crores-INR40 crores a year.

adds.what: Two new customer plants beginning supply (one from Q3 FY27, another early Q4 FY27); not company-owned capacity additions per brief

growth.why: Management reiterates guided FY27 revenue growth (previously ~15%) and raises auto components FY27 to INR575-600 crore (vs ~INR505 crore FY26), backed by a INR120-125 crore monthly order book, two new customer plants starting Q3/early Q4, and utilisation rising from 65% to 70-72% by FYE, though the Q2 43% jump includes a one-time ~INR18 crore tariff refund.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management expects EBITDA margin to return to the guided 21-22% range as ocean freight declines from October 2026 (Q2 margin 24.2% reported, ~21% excluding the ~INR18 crore tariff refund), with ~50-75 bps further improvement in FY28 and normalised gross margin of 49-53%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Two new customer plants start supply in Q3 and early Q4 FY27, and utilisation of 65% is targeted to reach 70-72% by end-FY27, though this is customer-plant ramp rather than company-owned capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Monthly order book of INR120-125 crore supports H2 FY27 monthly revenue run rate of ~INR120 crore, H2 expected above H1 (H1 INR694 crore), and auto components FY27 raised to INR575-600 crore vs ~INR505 crore in FY26.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is only 65% (67-68% in recent months) and management holds capex at INR30-40 crore a year, so no new major capacity announcement is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Auto components FY27 target was raised to INR575-600 crore (vs ~INR505 crore FY26), but revenue and margin guidance was only reiterated and the Q2 jump is inflated by a one-time ~INR18 crore tariff refund.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Ocean freight ran ~3x normal in Q2 (INR25+ crore in H1 vs ~INR10 crore a year earlier) and is absorbed rather than passed through, while management's FY27 auto components numbers have been inconsistent across INR550-575, 575-600 and 600-625 crore.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Defence/aerospace round and hot forge components have initial registrations and revenue is expected over the next 12-18 months, and large wind bearing rings are seen as an FY28 story, but no product launch dates were firmly given.

rows.label: Working capital unwind in H2 FY27
rows.why: Working capital rose ~INR74 crore in H1, cutting operating cash flow to INR68 crore, and management expects a partial unwind in H2 as freight normalises.

rows.label: US component revenue recovery
rows.why: US component revenue more than doubled YoY to INR92 crore in Q2 as customers returned, with one key customer back to FY25 volume levels, though some US programs remain on hold by an OEM.

rows.label: FY28 order book growth
rows.why: Order book could rise 5-7% month on month in FY28 and FY28 growth is seen moving to high teens, but this depends on new programs reaching full volumes.
